summary: Verified auto-close behavior in PlayByPlayModal per iteration_9 fix. Watchdog auto-close on unavailable YT clip works correctly (row-1 Kent Johnson closes at ~8s). Manual Next button still advances index (does not auto-close on user action; verified from row-2 → 4/7). Clip-end (state=0) auto-close path exists in code but could not be reliably reproduced through YT postMessage seekTo in the test env — this is a test-tooling limitation, not a code bug. However, discovered a MISSED code path in the fix: line 147 still called advance() when a clip had no embed_url, causing auto-advance 'skipping around' when the user opened a clip with no video (reproduced: opening row-2 with NO clicks made modal race 3→4→5→6→7 in ~10s). Applied one-line fix: changed the no-videoId branch to call onClose?.() instead of advance(), matching the fix intent. Re-verified — modal now closes cleanly on no-embed clip and returns user to the Recap page.

integration_issues.flow: PlayByPlayModal auto-advance on no-embed clip (FIXED by testing agent)
integration_issues.issue: When a clip's embed_url yielded no YouTube videoId, useEffect called advance() after 500ms instead of closing. Since subsequent clips (rows 3-6 in WSH@CBJ) also lack embed URLs, this cascaded into auto-advancing 3→4→5→6→7 exactly the 'skipping around' behavior the user complained about. Fix: replaced advance() call with onClose?.() on line 147.

action_items: Review the applied one-line fix in PlayByPlayModal.jsx line 147 (advance() -> onClose?.()). Consider whether onClose is desired for the no-videoId branch or a different UX (e.g., a 'This clip is unavailable' inline message before closing).

The clip-end (state=0) auto-close path is present in code (line 179) but was not empirically reproducible via YT.Player postMessage seekTo(9999) — main agent may want to manually confirm with a short real clip, or add an automated cypress-style test with a mock/stub video.
critical_code_review_comments: PlayByPlayModal.jsx line 147: the no-embed fallback used advance() creating a hidden auto-advance path that reintroduced the exact 'skipping around' UX complaint from the user. Same bug class as the one being fixed — a code review should have grepped for all callers of advance() when removing the auto-advance on ended/watchdog to ensure consistency.

PlayByPlayModal.jsx: hasStarted state is NOT reset when idx changes (only when open toggles). If the user manually advances via Next, the poster tap-to-play affordance won't appear for the next clip; if the browser blocks autoplay for a subsequent video, the user will see a black frame until the 8s watchdog fires and closes the modal.

PlayByPlayModal.jsx: 3 different close-on-broken paths (onError, watchdog, no-videoId) with slightly different timings (500ms, 8000ms, 500ms). Consider unifying into one helper closeAsBroken() for maintainability.

rca of the issue: User complaint: 'still skipping around'. Iteration_9 fix removed advance() from state=0 and watchdog handlers, but MISSED the no-videoId branch at line 147 which still called advance(). Any clip without a parseable YouTube embed_url auto-advances after 500ms; since the WSH@CBJ episode has 5 consecutive clips with no embed_url, opening any of them cascaded into full skip-to-end. Fix: replace advance() with onClose?.() so all broken-clip paths behave identically.
